bundles.question: What is the latest stable (general availability) version number of the Python programming language as listed by the official Python release/download information? (Use the current latest stable/GA release on python.org, not betas/rcs.)
bundles.summary: Official Python download pages show different “latest” values by page/component. The Windows “Stable Releases” section lists **Python 3.14.8** (Sept. 30, 2026) as the latest stable release [https://www.python.org/downloads/windows]. The main “Download Python” page shows **Latest: Python 3.14.7** [https://www.python.org]. The “Python Source Releases” page lists **Latest Python 3 Release - Python 3.14.7** [https://www.python.org/downloads/source]. Based on the Windows stable release listing, the latest stable/GA version number is **Python 3.14.8** [https://www.python.org/downloads/windows].
gaps: The question asks for the latest stable/GA version as listed by the official Python release/download information; the main downloads page indicates “Latest: Python 3.14.7” [https://www.python.org], while the Windows stable releases page lists “Python 3.14.8” [https://www.python.org/downloads/windows]. Need confirmation of which specific “official Python release/download information” section the question intends (e.g., top-level downloads vs. platform-specific stable releases).

No single python.org download listing in the provided results explicitly states that Python 3.14.8 is the overall latest stable/GA release across all platforms; source releases page still shows Python 3.14.7 as latest [https://www.python.org/downloads/source].
